subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Positive Reciprocity
description: A short lesson to help you apply Positive Reciprocity.

hook.text: Waiters who left a mint with the bill got 3% higher tips. Two mints got 14%. A personalized mint got 23%.

buildup.text: Positive reciprocity: when someone gives us something, we feel compelled to give back. The urge is automatic.

discovery.text: Regan's study showed that people who received a small unsolicited favor bought twice as many raffle tickets.

twist.text: The gift doesn't need to match. A small favor can trigger a disproportionately large return.

climax.text: Free samples, gifts, and favors exploit this. Be aware when generosity precedes a sales pitch. The debt is the product.

punchline.text: The free gift is never free. It buys your reciprocity.

quiz.question: What happens when a small unsolicited favor is given?
options: People feel no obligation to reciprocate
People often return a disproportionately large favor
People always return the exact same value
